newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CS sugar areas to stay hot until September.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CS sugar areas to stay hot until September.

text.p: Hot, dry weather should persist throughout the sugar cane growing region in Brazil's center-south until September, independent consultant DataNet-AgriCommodities said in a bulletin.

The El Nino weather system was preventing cold air masses from entering the southeast by intensifying high-altitude winds, and this was likely to keep temperatures high in sugar producing areas through July, August and September.
However, cold fronts could still enter the region at short notice so that close monitoring of the situation was needed.
The current high temperatures, coupled with moist soil, were not favoring the maturation of the sugar cane and sugar content had not risen as originally hoped in July, DataNet said.
It noted that heavy rains in the first two months of 1997 were keeping soil humid, despite the lack of rains during the last five weeks.

"In some cane areas between the north of Sao Paulo and the south of Minas Gerais a drop in minimum temperatures, which made early morning colder, could create better conditions for the maturation of the cane," DataNet said.
